title: Squares and notation

D0.outcome: Says what a file, a rank and a square name such as e4 are, and which colour the corner a1 is.

D1.outcome: Given a square name, taps that square on a board shown from White's side or from Black's side.

D2.outcome: Names any square pointed at, on a board with no labels and from either side, quickly and without counting.

D3.outcome: Without a board, says whether two squares share a rank, a file or a diagonal and names the squares between them.

misconceptions: Mixing up which comes first in a square name (the file letter, then the rank number).
Reading square names the wrong way round when the board is shown from Black's side.
conditions: A square name is the file letter first, then the rank number: e4 is file e, rank 4.
The names belong to the squares, not to the screen: when the board is turned to Black's side the names stay on the same squares.
contrasts: Reading e4 as rank e and file 4 puts the piece on a different square.
A board drawn with or without coordinate labels: the square is the same.
